established: Deduplication concept validated analytically on synthetic 32-task corpus: parameterized representation yields 25 vs 32 mechanisms (21.9% reduction) and 679 vs 791 tokens (0.8584 dedup ratio, 112 tokens/14.16% net savings) because 3 of 25 patterns are shared across 2-5 tasks

Per-task economics: shared patterns incur -15.8% per-task penalty (parameterized costs MORE per task due to ${slot} syntax overhead), but corpus savings arise from storing the pattern once instead of N times
Null-control overhead quantified: unique patterns show 25.3% token penalty (isolated ratio 1.253) from ${slot} syntax, establishing the breakeven threshold for deduplication viability
Sharing distribution characterized: 22/25 patterns are singleton (no dedup benefit), 1 pattern shared by 2 tasks, 1 by 3, 1 by 5 — only 12% of patterns provide dedup benefit
